3.1.2.locator: Security page, encryption section: 'sensitive data, like connection strings and settings, is encrypted at row-level with AES256 + SHA512'; 'AWS also encrypts the disks where data is written'
3.1.2.notes: Snippet-sourced (direct fetch blocked). Scope caveat: the documented AES-256 (AES256 + SHA512, row-level) applies specifically to sensitive data such as connection strings and settings; other at-rest data relies on AWS disk-level encryption whose algorithm Metabase's page does not itself specify (do not infer AWS's AES-256 default per the no-inference rule). Mitigating architecture: Metabase keeps customer business data on the customer's own databases and, unless results caching is enabled, does not store query results on its side. Confirm full-scope at-rest algorithm with the vendor.

3.1.3.notes: Backups are documented (security page: daily backups and cross-zone replication of core databases, restore capability tested annually) but no Metabase page retrieved this session states the encryption standard applied to backups. 'Not known' is the playbook-expected common answer here. Searched metabase.com/security, /cloud, /docs (domain-restricted search); direct fetches blocked.

3.1.8.value:
Data-minimization architecture: customer business data stays on the customer's own databases; unless results caching is enabled, no data returned by the customer's database is stored on Metabase's side
Single-tenant isolation: each Metabase Cloud customer runs in its own container (no shared clusters); dedicated single-tenant cloud deployment available on request
Identifiable data in collected usage/telemetry data is hashed
All system calls are logged, monitored and audited, with alerting on calls that indicate a potential intrusion or exfiltration attempt
Independent application-level and infrastructure-level penetration tests several times a year, with findings prioritized and remediated
Daily backups and replication of core databases across zones; backup and restore capability tested annually for disaster recovery
Sub-processor oversight: control reviews of sub-processing vendors before use and at least annually; sub-processors bound to confidentiality commitments; customers notified of new sub-processors via the published list (metabase.com/hosting/subprocessors) with a 10-day objection window
DPA commitment to delete or return all Customer Personal Data at expiry/termination of the agreement (backup/archival copies deleted per retention schedule)
